narration.say: We hit an asteroid. Here's the scar.
A European probe just found a stadium-sized crater on it.
A NASA probe had hit it at six kilometers per second.
cues: A NASA probe had hit it at

narration.say: Its orbit got 33 minutes shorter, far more than predicted.
Why? The blast threw rubble backward, like rocket exhaust.
That recoil multiplied the push about three and a half times.
cues: about three and a half times.

narration.say: So the rubble did most of the pushing. Good news for planetary defense.
Follow Media Diet for the physics behind the headlines.

shots.beat: first frame / hook: illustration of Hera's view — Dimorphos with one face flattened into a stadium-sized crater, tumbling, boulders orbiting; "WE HIT AN ASTEROID. / HERE'S THE SCAR."
Hera (paper orbiter) photographs the moonlet; a paper stadium slides in beside the crater for scale; "stadium-sized crater" + ESA date chip
flashback 26 Sep 2022: NASA DART streaks in and hits the round, pre-impact Dimorphos; flash and first ejecta; "6.1 km/s"
orbit: Dimorphos circles Didymos; the path tightens (gap exaggerated); "orbit: 33 min shorter"
mechanism: slow-motion plume of rubble blasted back out of the impact face like rocket exhaust; the asteroid recoils the other way; "rubble recoil"
sum of pushes: DART arrow (1×) + rubble recoil (≈2.6×) = ≈3.6× (β = 3.61, Cheng et al. 2023)
payoff: paper bars, DART vs rubble — the rubble did most of the pushing
planetary defence illustration: a generic incoming asteroid nudged by a probe misses a paper Earth
CTA: Media Diet sign flips up
